chunks.text: Definition. The average velocity of an object over a time interval is its displacement divided by the elapsed time: v_avg = Δx / Δt. Velocity is a vector, so its sign gives the direction of motion along the axis.

The instantaneous velocity is the limit of the average velocity as the time interval shrinks to zero, v = dx/dt. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, a = dv/dt, and it is also a vector quantity.
For constant acceleration the velocity changes linearly with time: v = v0 + a t, where v0 is the velocity at t = 0 and v is the velocity at time t.
The position then follows x = x0 + v0 t + (1/2) a t². Eliminating time between these equations gives v² = v0² + 2 a (x − x0), which links velocity and displacement directly.
Example 1.4 Free fall. A stone is released from rest. Taking upward as the positive direction, its acceleration is a = −g = −9.8 m/s², so its velocity becomes more negative as it falls.
Exercise 1.1 A ball is dropped from rest from a height of 20 m. How long does it take to reach the ground? Take g = 9.8 m/s².
Exercise 1.2 A car moving at 10 m/s accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s² for 5 s. Find its final speed and the distance it covers.
Definition. Newton's first law: an object at rest stays at rest, and an object in uniform motion stays in uniform motion along a straight line, unless a net external force acts on it.
A frame of reference in which the first law holds is called an inertial frame. Any frame moving at constant velocity relative to an inertial frame is also inertial.
Newton's second law: the net force on an object equals its mass times its acceleration, ΣF = m a. The acceleration points in the same direction as the net force.
In its more general form the second law reads ΣF = dp/dt, where p = m v is the momentum. This reduces to ΣF = m a when the mass is constant.
Example 2.3 A 5 kg crate is pulled by a rope with a net force of 20 N. Its acceleration is a = F/m = 4 m/s².
Exercise 2.1 A 2 kg mass accelerates at 3 m/s². Find the net force acting on it.
Exercise 2.2 Prove that an object moving at constant velocity has zero net force acting on it.
Definition. Friction is the contact force that opposes relative sliding between two surfaces. Its magnitude is f = μ N, where μ is the coefficient of friction and N is the normal force.
Static friction adjusts up to a maximum value μs N to prevent sliding, while kinetic friction has the constant magnitude μk N once the surfaces slide, and μk is usually smaller than μs.
